steps.summary: A self-guided training course for teachers new to Moodle. Learn how to create courses, add activities, manage students, and use the gradebook.

steps.name: Course Creation
steps.intro:
Module 1: Course Creation

Learn the fundamentals of creating and configuring courses in Moodle.

steps.name: Guide: Creating Your First Course
steps.intro: This guide walks you through creating a new course in Moodle. Topics covered: navigating to Site Administration > Courses > Add a new course, setting the course full name and short name, choosing a course format (weekly, topics, social), configuring enrollment methods, and setting course start and end dates. Tip: Use the Topics format for self-paced courses and the Weekly format for scheduled courses.

steps.name: Adding Activities
steps.intro:
Module 2: Adding Activities & Resources

Discover the activity and resource types available in Moodle and when to use each one.

steps.name: Guide: Activities and Resources
steps.intro: Moodle offers many activity types. Key activities: Assignment (collect and grade student work), Forum (discussions and peer interaction), Quiz (auto-graded assessments), Workshop (peer assessment). Key resources: Page (inline content), File (downloadable documents), URL (external links), Label (section headings and descriptions), Folder (organized file collections), Book (multi-page content). To add an activity: turn on Edit mode, click 'Add an activity or resource' in the desired section, and configure the settings.

steps.name: Managing Students
steps.intro:
Module 3: Managing Students

Learn about enrollment methods, user roles, and group management.

steps.name: Guide: Enrollment and Groups
steps.intro: Student management in Moodle: Enrollment methods include manual enrollment (teacher adds students), self-enrollment (students enroll themselves with an optional key), and cohort sync (automatic enrollment from site-level groups). User roles: Manager, Course creator, Teacher (editingteacher), Non-editing teacher, Student, Guest. Groups: Create groups for team projects or differentiated instruction. Use Groupings to assign specific activities to specific groups. Access the Participants page from the course navigation to manage enrolled users.

steps.name: Assessment & Grades
steps.intro:
Module 4: Assessment & Grades

Master the gradebook and learn how to configure grading for your course.

steps.name: Guide: Grading and the Gradebook
steps.intro: The Moodle Gradebook automatically collects grades from all graded activities. Key concepts: Grade categories (organize grades into weighted groups), Grade calculations (weighted mean, simple weighted mean, natural), Grade letters (customize the A-F scale), Grading workflows (enable draft grades before releasing to students), Rubrics and Marking guides (create structured grading criteria for assignments). Access the gradebook from Course navigation > Grades. Set up your grade structure early in the course to avoid recalculation issues later.
